selected_evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3)
selected_evidence.summary: opt1/opt2 interfaces on node1 came up with correct IPs matching node2/node3 segments; node2 successfully pings across node1 to node3's lan-b address, proving routing works.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2->node3 (lan-a to lan-b) traffic appears at node3 as originating from a chosen address on node1, not node2's own address
selected_evidence.summary: Outbound NAT rule added (source 192.168.10.0/24 on opt2 -> target 192.168.20.1) and loaded into pf. tcpdump on node1's vtnet2 (lan-b wire) during a node2->node3 ping shows packets as '192.168.20.1 > 192.168.20.2', i.e. sourced from node1's opt2 address rather than node2's 192.168.10.2.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3->node2 (lan-b to lan-a) traffic keeps its original source address (no NAT applied in that direction)
selected_evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's vtnet1 (lan-a wire) during a node3->node2 ping shows packets as '192.168.20.2 > 192.168.10.2', proving node3's real address is preserved when reaching node2 -- confirming the NAT rule only applies to the lan-a-to-lan-b direction.

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline behavior before NAT was added (falsification / control)
selected_evidence.summary: Before the outbound NAT rule existed, tcpdump on node1's vtnet2 during node2->node3 ping showed the un-NATed flow as '192.168.10.2 > 192.168.20.2', proving the later SNAT behavior is caused by the added rule and not pre-existing routing behavior.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 9feeb0bb.../uptime pre-restart, issued native reboot, confirmed exec unreachable mid-restart, polled until boot_id changed to 6e496c6a... (proving a real restart), then confirmed enp8s0 static IP/routes and lan-b reachability recovered.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 31949c21.../uptime pre-restart, issued native reboot, confirmed exec unreachable mid-restart, polled until boot_id changed to 184a3590... (proving a real restart), then confirmed enp8s0 static IP/routes and lan-a reachability recovered.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 (OPNsense router) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state including persisted NAT config
selected_evidence.summary: Captured kern.boottime (17:28:39) pre-restart, issued native FreeBSD reboot, confirmed SSH/exec unreachable mid-restart, polled until kern.boottime changed to 17:34:29 (proving a real restart), then confirmed opt1/opt2 interfaces and the outbound NAT rule persisted from config.xml after reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Full asymmetric NAT behavior re-verified end-to-end after all three node restarts
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart, repeated the tcpdump verification: node2->node3 traffic on vtnet2 still shows source 192.168.20.1 (SNAT active), and node3->node2 traffic on vtnet1 still shows source 192.168.20.2 (no NAT), confirming the configuration and its asymmetric behavior survived all three node restarts.
